artifacts.summary: Confirms the cited miss's phase genuinely carried the Batch Gate Deferral obligation (final, full-tier phase); recommends Option 1 (hoist the section after ## Description) over Option 2 (structurally unavailable for the non-hard-mode dispatch shape that failed) and Option 3 (blocked today by stale, never-cleaned-up multi-task state files causing false-positive risk); reconciles with completed task 445 (no conflict, disjoint mechanism); points to an existing Group 15 test idiom for the required position-pinning fixture.

memory_candidates.content: In this agent-system's orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh, '## Phase Mission' is emitted only when $phase_number is set, which is exclusively an H1 hard-mode per-phase-dispatch construct. An ordinary (non-hard-mode) implement dispatch processes ALL plan phases inside one dispatch via general-implementation-agent.md's own internal phase loop, with no per-phase dispatch-file section. Any design proposing to 'restate a directive in the final phase's dispatch-file section' must check which dispatch shape (hard vs. ordinary) actually produced the incident it targets, since the section may not exist in the common case.

specs/.orchestration/.orchestrator-multi-state-<session_id>.json files (the multi-task batch state file, path from runtime_mt_state_path() in scripts/lib/runtime-file-patterns.sh) are never cleaned up after a batch /orchestrate invocation completes -- no rm call exists in orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, or skill-orchestrate.sh. Any future mechanism that wants to detect 'is there an active multi-task batch right now' by checking for this file's existence will false-positive against stale leftovers (8 observed in one live repository, spanning several days) unless it also threads the invoking session_id through and adds a liveness signal beyond mere presence.

test-orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh (Group 15, Case 2) already has a reusable position-pinning idiom for asserting one dispatch-file section is emitted before another: grep -n '^## HeadingA' and grep -n '^## HeadingB' on the composed dispatch file, cut -d: -f1 each to a line number, then a numeric -lt comparison with a named pass/fail. Reuse this idiom verbatim for any future 'section X must precede section Y' dispatch-file ordering fixture rather than inventing a new technique.
